question: If a conductor moves through a uniform magnetic field, the induced potential difference is maximised when _____.

options.text: the conductor is parallel to the magnetic field lines
the conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field lines

solution:
The correct answer is __the conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field lines****.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Induced potential difference__ depends on the relative motion between the conductor and the magnetic field.
 
• It is maximized when the conductor cuts the magnetic field lines at a right angle (perpendicular).
 
• When the conductor is parallel to the magnetic field lines, no potential difference is induced.
 
• The induced potential difference is proportional to the velocity of motion, magnetic field strength, and the angle of intersection.
 
• This principle is based on Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Faraday's Law:**
 
 
• It states that a changing magnetic field induces an electromotive force (EMF) in a conductor.
 
• The induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of the magnetic flux through the conductor.
 
 
 
• **Lenz's Law:**
 
 
• The direction of induced current opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it.
 
• This ensures the principle of conservation of energy.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Electric generators work on the principle of electromagnetic induction.
 
• Transformers use induction to transfer energy between coils.
